//: Reference for every setting the portal understands. Copy the values you need into
environment variables or a secret store — never commit real secrets.
Environment variables use double underscores for nesting:

ConnectionStrings.//Sentinel: Wins over Database:ConnectionString. Supply it as a secret, never in a file.

Database.//Provider: PostgreSql | Sqlite | SqlServer. Sqlite is for local development and tests only.
Database.//MigrateOnStartup: Fine for a single instance. With replicas, migrate as a deployment step.
Database.//EnableSensitiveDataLogging: Logs query parameter values. Rejected outright in Production.

Security.//RequireHttps: Forces HTTPS redirection, HSTS, Secure cookies and the __Host- cookie prefix.
Security.//ForwardedHeaderHops: Number of trusted reverse proxies. 0 disables X-Forwarded-* handling.

LoginRateLimit.//: Per source address, on top of Identity's per-account lockout.

SecurityHeaders.//ContentSecurityPolicyReportOnly: Report violations without enforcing. Use while tightening a policy.

Membership.//GracePeriodDays: Days of access after expiry so a late renewal does not lock a customer out.

Features.//: Switching a feature off closes its server endpoints (they answer 404), not merely its menu link.
Features.//ProductDiscoveryEnabled: Off makes the portal invitation-only: members still see My Library, but cannot browse what they do not have.
Features.//BetaProductsEnabled: Off withdraws pre-release products from the catalogue. Members already invited keep their access.
Features.//financial: These stay false until the purchase and wallet code has had its own security review. Do not enable in production before then.

SuperAdmin.//: Bootstraps the first administrator. A no-op once any SuperAdmin exists.
SuperAdmin.//Password: Supply through Seed__SuperAdmin__Password only. Clear it after first boot.

Seed.//IncludeSampleApplications: Placeholder catalogue rows for local development. Rejected in Production.

ExpiryNotices.//: Recurring sweep that warns members about membership and subscription expiry.
ExpiryNotices.//IntervalMinutes: Expiry is measured in days, so hourly is plenty; finer only adds load.
ExpiryNotices.//StartupDelaySeconds: Keeps a restart — or a crash loop — from turning into a burst of messages.
ExpiryNotices.//BatchSize: Subjects examined per sweep, per kind. Leftovers are picked up next time.
ExpiryNotices.//QuotaWarningPercent: Percentage of a subscription's data used before a warning is raised.

Subscriptions.//: Server-side fetching of subscription links. Turn Enabled off to remove the feature entirely.
Subscriptions.//MaxResponseBytes: Hard cap on the body. A subscription is a few kilobytes; anything larger is not one.
Subscriptions.//MaxRedirects: Each hop is re-validated against the same rules as the original URL.
Subscriptions.//CacheMinutes: How long a fetched result is reused. Also the floor on how often a member can make the server reach out.
Subscriptions.//UserAgent: Many panels return a different format per user agent, so this is configurable.

Panel.//: 3x-ui panels the portal provisions against. Each server is a row in the admin UI, not a setting here — only the client's own behaviour is configured.
Panel.//HealthCheckIntervalMinutes: How often each panel is re-probed. 0 disables the sweep, which leaves a dead panel in selection.
Panel.//insecure: Both refused in Production. http would put the panel's API token — full control of that panel — on the wire in the clear; loopback exists so the test suite can reach a fake panel.

Provisioning.//: The background workers that turn a queued service into a client on a panel. Every replica runs them; claiming a job is a guarded write, so exactly one replica executes each.
Provisioning.//Enabled: Set false only when the workers run in a separate process. Off here with nothing else running them leaves every new service stuck in Pending.
Provisioning.//jobs: A queued job is a customer waiting for their first configuration, so this sweep is frequent. The batch size bounds how many panel round trips one sweep can make.
Provisioning.//usage: Traffic counters, in minutes rather than seconds: a quota measured in gigabytes does not change meaningfully inside a minute, and polling every service constantly is a lot of panel load for no extra accuracy.
Provisioning.//reconcile: Resolves services parked because a panel write ended without an answer. Such a write is never retried — the sweep reads the panel to establish what actually happened first. Each parked service is a customer in limbo, so keep this frequent.

Telegram.//: Optional. With Enabled false the whole integration is dormant and notifications stay in the portal.
Telegram.//BotToken: A full credential — supply through Telegram__BotToken only. Never in a file, never logged.
Telegram.//BotUsername: Without the @. Used to build the https://t.me/<bot>?start=... deep link.
Telegram.//PublicBaseUrl: Absolute origin of the portal, so notification links work inside Telegram.
Telegram.//UsePolling: Long polling. Works without any inbound route; a webhook would need one plus its own secret path.
Telegram.//DeliveryBatchSize: Messages per sweep. Telegram throttles bulk sends, so a broadcast is paced rather than fired at once.

DataProtection.//KeyRingPath: Mount a volume here so cookies survive a container redeploy. Empty = in-process keys.
